newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Dec CPI rises a higher than expected 4.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai Dec CPI rises a higher than expected 4.8 pct.

text.p: Thailand's consumer price index (CPI) rose a slightly higher-than-expected 4.8 percent year-on-year in December, unchanged from November, but sharply up from the 2.9 percent increase recorded in December 1995.

The commerce ministry said on Thursday the overall 1996 CPI increase hit a six-year high of 5.9 percent against 5.8 percent in 1995. The 1996 overall figure was also a touch higher than the 5.8 percent estimated by the central bank last week.
The ministry said, however, that the 1990-based index eased 0.1 percent month-on-month in December to 136.3, largely on declining food prices, after a 0.5 percent month-on-month increase in November.
The ministry said vegetable and fruit prices fell 3.4 percent in December after a 2.1 percent decline in November.

An analyst at Dhana Siam Finance said 1990-1994 records showed that the CPI registered an average 0.2 percent month-on-month decline in November and December when fresh harvests of many key agricultural commodities reach the market.
The analyst had said, ahead of the inflation result, that December year-on-year inflation should come in lower than the 4.8 percent posted in November.

Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasenee said on Thursday he expects Thai inflation to face less upward pressure from oil prices in 1997 due to the U.N. decision to allow Iraq to resume oil exports from December 10.
Under the U.N. plan, Iraq will sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months.
